precepts.text: O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself, but in the Most High is thy help; we fell by following behind these other nations.
precepts.point: The word is to remove out of the midst of Babylon and go forth from the land of the Chaldeans, coming out of her ways and her religions and back to the commandments.

note.label: Jeremiah 50: The Fall of Babylon and the Return of Israel

precepts.why:
“O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help.” We fell by following behind these other nations. “My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray”: the so-called reverends and prosperity preachers are bald-headed, beardless, and do nothing the Bible says, turning the people from mountain to hill until they forget their resting place.

“All that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord”. Our enemies know that when Israel sins the Most High will not fight for us, and to some degree they are right. Israel destroyed itself.

But in him is our help, and that is the word: “Remove out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans”, coming out of her ways and her religions and back to the commandments.

precepts.text: The workman forms a graven image profitable for nothing, fashions it after the figure of a man, then burns part of the same wood for fire and falls down to worship the rest as a god.
precepts.point: Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men.

note.label: Hosea 13: In Me Is Thine Help

precepts.why:
“And now they sin more and more, and have made them molten images of their silver, and idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen”. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time. Isaiah shows what that craftsman was doing: “Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?” The workmen “are of men”.

The smith works it “with the strength of his arms”. The carpenter “marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.” The craftsman was making idols in the images of men.

He cuts down a tree, and “Then shall it be for a man to burn”; he warms himself and bakes bread with part of it, “yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it”. “He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh”, then “the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.” That is the idol according to their own understanding, profitable for nothing; and they say of them, let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves.

precepts.text: Even Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged that the God of Israel is the only true living God, a God of gods and a Lord of kings.
precepts.point: He will be thy king; where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities, and thy judges of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? The Lord is telling us there is none that saveth but him.

note.label: Hosea 13: In Me Is Thine Help

precepts.why:
“I will be thy king: where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities?” The Lord is telling us there is none that saveth but him. Even Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged it: “Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, seeing thou couldest reveal this secret.”

The God of Israel is the only true living God, a God of gods and a Lord of kings. There is no other king and no other judges, of whom they said give me a king and princes, that can save.

precepts.text: The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight, and there was none left but the tribe of Judah only, when the northern kingdom was carried out and heathen were placed in the land.
precepts.point: Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up. This was a future prophecy at the time Hosea prophesied, about Assyria coming into the land.

note.label: Hosea 13: In Me Is Thine Help

precepts.why:
“Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God”. At the time Hosea prophesied this was a future prophecy, about Assyria coming into the land: they would fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up.

2 Kings records it coming to pass. “Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.” The northern kingdom was carried out and heathen were placed in the land; Samaria became desolate as Hosea said.

Them that are bound: spiritual bondage, the enslavement of sin. “The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is hid.” Say that: the iniquity of Ephraim is bound up. His sin is hid.

From here to John 8:32, because we always read that one: the truth shall make you free, and when Christ says that he's talking about two things, a literal meaning and a spiritual meaning.

points: O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself. We destroyed ourselves because we've been depending on this nation to help us, like Proverbs 13:12 says, hope deferred maketh the heart sick. We looking for change and no change coming.

But in me is thine help. In the Lord is our help. We got to come back to this Bible, y'all; that's the only change we going to have. Everything here is for our demise. The only thing that is not for our demise is this Bible, and that's what's protecting all of us who keep the law of commandments in sincerity.
